proof_summary: Let \(r\in[1/2,1]\) satisfy \(H(r)=r\log 2\), where \(H\) is binary entropy; bounding each residue by both \(2^k\) and \(\binom nk\) gives \(a(n)\le n\exp(nH(r))\). For the reverse exponential bound, choose \(k=\lfloor yn\rfloor\) with \(y>r\) arbitrarily close to \(r\): then \(H(y)<y\log2\), so eventually \(\binom nk<2^k\) and that residue equals \(\binom nk\), while the entropy lower bound \(\binom nk\ge \exp(nH(k/n))/(n+1)\) shows \(\log a(n)/n\to H(r)\), hence the roots tend to \(e^{H(r)}=2^r\).
